situation:
You are the human resources manager at CROSSWIND REGIONAL AIRWAYS, a two-year-old airline flying fourteen turboprops between small cities. The chief operating officer (judge) has asked you to bring a recommendation to this week's leadership meeting.

CROSSWIND REGIONAL AIRWAYS is spending the last of the money it raised at launch, and the investors who funded it expect the airline to reach its next funding milestone on what remains. It recruited its pilots and mechanics away from larger carriers with one thing those carriers would not offer: health coverage for the whole family at no cost to the employee. The airline recruits on that promise and markets on it, in hiring notices and on the routes alike.

The benefits package renews next month at thirty-one percent above what the airline paid this year. Renewing it as it stands takes roughly three months out of the runway left before the funding milestone. The plan the broker offers instead costs less than this year's package and moves employees to a high deductible with a monthly premium share, so crews would pay for coverage for the first time.

The first six routes have moved out of their launch phase into steady demand, fares on them are softening, and the marketing that once sold a new route now sells the airline itself. The chief operating officer (judge) wants you to analyze the choice and recommend one course, knowing that the cheaper plan gives up the promise the airline recruits and markets on, and that renewing as it stands spends runway the airline may not get back.

You will present your recommendation to the chief operating officer (judge) in a meeting to take place in his/her office. The chief operating officer (judge) will begin the meeting by greeting you and asking to hear your ideas. After you have presented and have answered the chief operating officer's (judge) questions, the chief operating officer (judge) will thank you for your work.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the chief operating officer (judge) of CROSSWIND REGIONAL AIRWAYS. Business background is the same as the situation above. The benefits renewal lands next month, the airline has to reach its funding milestone on the money it has left, and the coverage in question is the reason most of the crews are here rather than at a larger carrier.

You want the human resources manager to analyze the choice and recommend whether to renew the package as it stands or move to the cheaper plan, and to say what the airline gives up either way.

During the presentation you are to ask the following questions of the participant:
judgeQuestions: Two years from now, what would this decision have changed about who works here?
What happens at the next renewal if the cost goes up again?
